speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To better understand your symptoms, when did your double vision and weakness first start, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. To narrow this down further, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or breathing shortness of breath? Also, how old are you?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC, Electrolytes, and Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies. Also, please tell me if you experience any ptosis or difficulty lifting your arms overhead? REQUEST IMAGES: EMG_Nerve_Conduction, MRI_Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: NORMAL READINGS; Electrolytes: NORMAL READINGS; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Ptosis: Present (drooping of the right upper eyelid that worsens with sustained upward gaze); Difficulty lifting arms: Diminished motor strength observed in the upper extremities; EMG_Nerve_Conduction: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; MRI_Brain: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fluctuating weakness, ptosis that worsens with gaze, and positive acetylcholine receptor antibodies strongly indicates Myasthenia Gravis. Given your difficulty climbing stairs and upper limb weakness, I am concerned about potential respiratory muscle involvement; do you experience any shortness of breath, especially when lying flat or climbing stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. Given the confirmed elevated antibodies, characteristic ptosis, and fatigable weakness without respiratory distress, your condition appears stable for now; I recommend starting with low-dose prednisone and scheduling follow-up in two weeks to monitor for bulbar or respiratory progression.
